clue.text: Notes stammer when speaking to a debt dodger

indicators.note: the stammer word is to be heard rather than read, so its spelling can change

blocks.note: two musical notes of the scale
to falter is to stammer or hesitate in speech

explanation.surface: Someone stammers nervously when confronting a person who has dodged paying a debt.
explanation.walkthrough: Any two notes from A to G will do; here D and E, followed by a word that sounds like falter.
explanation.definitionFit: A defaulter fails to pay what is owed, so the term suits someone who dodges a debt.

clue.text: Chanced getting a hat trick of diamonds

blocks.note: three ways of writing diamonds: D, then ICE (slang for diamonds), then D again

explanation.surface: A card player takes a gamble and is dealt three diamonds in a row.
explanation.walkthrough: A hat trick is three of something; diamonds here is given three times, as the card-suit letter D, the slang ICE, and D once more.
explanation.definitionFit: To dice, as in diced with death, is to gamble or take a risk, so diced means took a chance.

clue.text: Naval unit, heading for Deal, say, makes port

blocks.note: a fleet is a group of naval ships
deal is fir or pine timber, an example of wood

explanation.surface: A squadron of warships sails towards the Kentish town of Deal and reaches harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: Deal is a Kent seaside town, which makes it look like a place, but lower-case deal is softwood timber; 'say' marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Fleetwood is a fishing and ferry harbour town on the Lancashire coast of England.

clue.text: A club is one place out of order for this type

definitions.note: the answer is an adjective describing the type

indicators.note: to place things out of order is to set them in a new jumbled sequence

blocks.note: taken as written, ten letters

explanation.surface: Someone who would think joining a club out of place, the sort who avoids company.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on the whole clue: the type for whom a club is one place to avoid.
explanation.definitionFit: An unsociable person dislikes company and gatherings, exactly the kind who shuns clubs and societies.

clue.text: Handicap by turning right and heading back

indicators.note: turning round makes the abbreviation for right run the other way
going back means the word for heading is read from its end to its start

blocks.note: RT is a standard abbreviation for right
a lemma is the heading word of a dictionary entry or annotation

explanation.surface: A vehicle is hampered by having to turn right and then head back the way it came.
explanation.walkthrough: A lemma is the headword or title of an entry, a fairly rare sense of heading.
explanation.definitionFit: A trammel is a hindrance or restraint, and as a verb to trammel is to hamper or impede.

clue.text: Put up ally in Queen's Suite

indicators.note: in places the word for ally inside the letters for Queen
in a down clue, putting something up reads it from bottom to top

blocks.note: ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen
to ally is to join together

explanation.surface: A friend is given lodging in the royal suite of rooms.
explanation.walkthrough: Suite looks like a set of rooms, but it is the train of attendants following a monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: A suite in the older sense is a group of followers or attendants, which is what a retinue is.

clue.text: Painter's in bilge, we're told

indicators.note: being told something means hearing it spoken, so the word for bilge is heard

blocks.note: bilge and bosh are both slang for nonsense

explanation.surface: A painter is stuck in the foul water at the bottom of a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: Bilge looks like ship's water; here it is nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: Hieronymus Bosch was a Dutch artist famous for his crowded, fantastical religious paintings.

clue.text: Blood money paid in Chicago

blocks.note: first meaning: a dashing young man about town
second meaning: American slang for a dollar

explanation.surface: A gangland payment in Chicago for a killing.
explanation.walkthrough: Blood money suggests a hitman's fee, but blood is a separate meaning: an old word for a spirited young man.
explanation.definitionFit: Buck and blood are both dated words for a fashionable young fellow, and buck is American slang for a dollar.

clue.text: That is low - could be lower

indicators.note: could be suggests the word low might become another arrangement of itself

blocks.note: sc. abbreviates scilicet, Latin for that is to say
taken as written

explanation.surface: A remark that something is low, and might yet go lower still.
explanation.walkthrough: Lower here rhymes with flower, not with slower: it is a verb meaning to frown.
explanation.definitionFit: To lower, rhyming with tower, is to frown or look sullen and threatening, the same as to glower.

clue.text: Largely low shelter restyled for this person

indicators.note: largely means most but not all, so the last letter of low is dropped
restyled means given a new form, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written before trimming
taken as written

explanation.surface: A modest, low-lying shelter has been remodelled to suit a particular guest.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition points back at the shelter in the surface: the person it is restyled for is one who stays in hostels.
explanation.definitionFit: A hosteller is someone who lodges at youth hostels, the cheap shelters used by travellers and walkers.

clue.text: Climbs with limbs special to these insects

indicators.note: special asks for a more particular word in place of limbs within climbs

blocks.note: taken as written
legs are the particular limbs used for walking

explanation.surface: Insects that clamber about using legs specially adapted for climbing.
explanation.walkthrough: Climbs ends in the letters limbs; swap those for legs and C is left at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Clegs are horseflies, biting flies that pester livestock and people in summer.

clue.text: Tossed out this sort of clue about sport

indicators.note: tossed means thrown about, so the letters of out land in a new order
about means going round, so the clue type wraps the other piece

blocks.note: taken as written
the clue itself is an across clue in the grid

explanation.surface: Someone throws out a crossword clue about a sport as unfair.
explanation.walkthrough: This sort of clue refers to its own grid direction; the setter is pointing at the label printed above it.
explanation.definitionFit: Autocross is a motor sport in which cars race against the clock round a rough grass or dirt track.

clue.text: Military unit seeking engagement? Quite the opposite

blocks.note: first meaning: a group of troops sent off on a separate task
second meaning: aloofness, the reverse of involvement

explanation.surface: A body of troops looking to engage the enemy, or not.
explanation.walkthrough: Engagement suggests battle with the military unit, but the second half wants its opposite in the sense of involvement: standing apart.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a separated body of soldiers and also emotional aloofness, the reverse of being engaged or involved.

clue.text: Sad blow

blocks.note: first meaning: feeling low
second meaning: to squander money

explanation.walkthrough: Blow looks like a noun, a setback; it is the verb, to spend recklessly, which old British slang also expresses with the answer word.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means melancholy, and in dated British slang to blue money is to waste or squander it.

clue.text: One has The Times ordered

blocks.note: surface reading: someone with a newspaper on order from the newsagent
setter's reading: a person who sets past times in sequence, a historian of events

explanation.surface: A reader has arranged for The Times to be delivered each morning.
explanation.walkthrough: The capitals make it the newspaper; read lower case, it is times placed in chronological order.
explanation.definitionFit: A chronicler records events in the order they happened, so the times of history are set out in sequence.

clue.text: Not a shoemaker's tool heard in making clever clogs

indicators.note: heard means the words are taken by their sound and respelt

blocks.note: an awl is a pointed tool cobblers use to pierce leather

explanation.surface: A cobbler has no awl to hand while making a pair of wooden clogs.
explanation.walkthrough: Clever clogs is British slang for a smart alec, not footwear, though the shoemaker in the surface pushes you towards shoes.
explanation.definitionFit: Clever clogs is a British jibe for someone who shows off knowledge, exactly what a know-it-all does.

clue.text: Criminal traced to Leatherhead

blocks.note: kid is soft leather made from young goatskin; the town name Leatherhead splits in two
napper is British slang for the head

explanation.surface: Police track a criminal down to the Surrey town of Leatherhead.
explanation.walkthrough: Leatherhead is a real town in Surrey, but it splits into two words.
explanation.definitionFit: A kidnapper is a criminal who abducts someone, usually to hold them for ransom.

clue.text: Honourable, this Roman and others around

indicators.note: around means the phrase for and others is placed on either side of the Latin word

blocks.note: et al. abbreviates Latin et alii, and others
hic is Latin for this, as a Roman would say it

explanation.surface: A noble Roman and his companions are described as honourable men.
explanation.walkthrough: Roman tells you to put this into Latin.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethical means morally upright and principled, which is what an honourable person is.

clue.text: Exchanged views? That's taken for granted!

blocks.note: first meaning: talked things over
second meaning: bestowed, as a title or honour

explanation.surface: Someone discussed it, and now behaves as though the outcome were assured.
explanation.walkthrough: Taken for granted looks like an idiom for assumed, but only granted is the definition, in the sense of awarded.
explanation.definitionFit: To confer is to consult together, and also to bestow an honour or degree on someone.

clue.text: Falsifier of records given fresh start - and still he cheats

indicators.note: a fresh start means the opening letter is swapped for a different one

blocks.note: one who fiddles the books falsifies accounts

explanation.surface: A fraudster gets a new start in life, but carries on cheating.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening F is replaced by D; the new letter is not clued, only that the start changes.
explanation.definitionFit: To diddle is British slang for swindling, so a diddler is a cheat or con artist.

clue.text: Rover plant

blocks.note: first meaning: a wanderer
second meaning: a climbing rose

explanation.walkthrough: Rover suggests a dog or a car, but here it is someone who roams.
explanation.definitionFit: A rambler is a person who walks for pleasure in the country, and also a vigorous climbing rose.

clue.text: Bare all over the head? That's his hair all over the bed!

definitions.text: Bare all over the head? That's his hair all over the bed!

blocks.note: surface reading: someone completely bald

blocks.clueFragment: That's his hair all over the bed!
blocks.note: setter's reading: swapping the opening sounds of bare and head is the slip of the tongue named after an Oxford don

explanation.surface: A bald man, yet his hair is apparently strewn across the bed.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the first sounds of bare and head and you get hair and bed: the joke is a sample of the man's own famous verbal slip.
explanation.definitionFit: William Spooner, an Oxford warden, gave his name to swapping initial sounds of words in a phrase.

clue.text: Crew member checks mounting fear in different ways

indicators.note: mounting in a down clue means rising, so the word for fear reads upwards
in places the turned word inside the roads

blocks.note: awe is reverential fear
two different ways: ST for street and RD for road

explanation.surface: A member of a ship's crew keeps rising panic in check in various ways.
explanation.walkthrough: ST and RD are standard address abbreviations for street and road, two kinds of way.
explanation.definitionFit: A steward is an attendant on a ship or aircraft who looks after passengers, part of the crew.

clue.text: Old writer having ritual drink in retreat

indicators.note: retreating means going backwards, so the drink is read from end to start

blocks.note: soma is the ritual drink of ancient Vedic religion

explanation.surface: An ageing author takes a ceremonial drink while on a retreat.
explanation.walkthrough: Retreat suggests a quiet spiritual getaway, fitting the ritual drink, but it signals going backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Amos was a Hebrew prophet of the eighth century BC, and the Old Testament book is his writing.

clue.text: Animal, one of many in the pound

definitions.text: one of many in the pound

blocks.note: first meaning: the snow leopard

blocks.clueFragment: one of many in the pound
blocks.note: second meaning: a unit of weight, sixteen to the pound

explanation.surface: One of many stray animals held in the pound.
explanation.walkthrough: The pound looks like an animal enclosure; it is the weight.
explanation.definitionFit: The ounce is another name for the snow leopard, and sixteen ounces make one avoirdupois pound.

clue.text: Barrier to free speech?

blocks.note: surface reading: censorship restricting what people may say
setter's reading: a stammer or lisp stopping words from flowing freely

explanation.surface: A political obstacle to the right to say what you like.
explanation.walkthrough: Free speech is the civil liberty in the surface, but read literally it is speech that flows freely.
explanation.definitionFit: An impediment is an obstruction in general, and in particular a speech defect such as a stammer.

clue.text: Tea, say, lying on pit of stomach

indicators.note: say tells you to speak the word tea and use the letter it sounds like

blocks.note: the drink sounds like the letter
a pit is a hole in the ground

explanation.surface: A cup of tea sits heavy in the pit of someone's stomach.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, lying on means the first piece sits above the second. Pit of stomach is a phrase, but stomach stands alone as a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Thole is a Scots and northern word meaning endure or put up with, as to stomach something does.

clue.text: Tarry rope

blocks.note: first meaning: to linger
second meaning: a rope bracing a ship's mast

explanation.walkthrough: Tarry looks like an adjective, covered in tar as a ship's rope would be; it is the verb, to linger.
explanation.definitionFit: To stay is to remain or linger, and a stay is a strong rope supporting a mast on a sailing ship.

clue.text: Girl taking first puff without a smoke

indicators.note: without in its old sense means outside, so the puff goes around the letter
taking first means the girl has the other piece placed in front of her

blocks.note: to puff is to pant for breath
taken as written
a girl's name

explanation.surface: A young woman takes her first puff, though without any cigarette.
explanation.walkthrough: First puff suggests the first letter of puff, but first goes with taking: the girl takes a word for puff in front of her.
explanation.definitionFit: A panatella is a long thin cigar, and a cigar is a smoke in everyday speech.

clue.text: Slow passage of old ship on lake

blocks.note: L is the map abbreviation for lake
the Argo was Jason's ship in Greek legend

explanation.surface: An ancient vessel makes a leisurely crossing of a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: On means placed next to, so the ship follows the lake's letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Largo is a musical direction for a very slow, broad tempo, and a largo is a movement or passage so marked.

clue.text: Stalky and gannet-like, except for head

indicators.note: except for its head means everything apart from the opening letter is kept

blocks.note: a gannet is British slang for a greedy eater

explanation.surface: A seabird described as long-stemmed and gluttonous, apart from its head.
explanation.walkthrough: Gannet in British slang is someone who gobbles food.
explanation.definitionFit: Reedy means full of reeds or thin and stalk-like, like the tall slender stems of reeds.

clue.text: Flushed game in partly forested area of London

blocks.note: flushed in the face is red
bridge is a card game

explanation.surface: Game birds are flushed out of cover in a wooded corner of London.
explanation.walkthrough: Flushed game suggests shooting, driving birds into the air, but it is a colour and a card game.
explanation.definitionFit: Redbridge is an outer London borough that includes part of Epping Forest and Hainault Forest.
